text:
The dimensional formula of $\frac{1}{2}𝜖_{0}E^{2}$ ($𝜖_{0}$ = permittivity of vacuum and $E$ = electric field) is $M^{a}L^{b}T^{c}$.
The value of $2a-b+c=$ $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The expression given is $\frac{1}{2}ε_{0}E^{2}$, which represents the energy density ($U_{d}$) of an electric field in a vacuum.

Energy density is defined as the energy stored per unit volume.

$U_{d}=\frac{\text{Energy}(U)}{\text{Volume}(V)}$

Energy is equivalent to work done, which is Force $\times$ Displacement.

The dimensions of force is $[F]=[ma]=[MLT^{-2}]$

So, the dimensions of energy is $[U]=[MLT^{-2}]\times [L]=[ML^{2}T^{-2}]$

The dimensions of volume is $[V]=[L]\times [L]\times [L]=[L^{3}]$

Since energy density is $\frac{U}{V}$, its dimensions are:

$[U_{d}]=\frac{[ML^{2}T^{-2}]}{[L^{3}]}=[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$

The dimensional formula of energy density due to electric field is is $M^{a}L^{b}T^{c}$.

By comparing this with derived dimensional formula $[M^{1}L^{-1}T^{-2}]$, we get:

$a=1,b=-1,c=-2$

So, the value of $2a-b+c=2(1)-(-1)+(-2)=2+1-2=1$

Therefore, the value of $2a-b+c$ is 1. Thus, the correct options is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
The diameter of a wire measured by a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm is 0.08 cm. The length measured by a scale of least count 0.1 cm is 150 cm. When a weight of 100 N is applied to the wire, the extension in length is 0.5 cm, measured by a micrometer of least count 0.001 cm. The error in the measured Young’s modulus is $α\times 10^{9}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The value of $α$ is $________$.

(Ignore the contribution of the load to Young’s modulus error calculation)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Young's modulus $(Y)$ is defined as the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain.

Let $F$ be the force, $L$ the original length, $A$ the cross-sectional area, and $\Delta L$ the extension.

$Y=\frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}=\frac{F/A}{\Delta L/L}=\frac{FL}{A\Delta L}$

For a wire of diameter $D$, the area $A=\frac{πD^{2}}{4}$.

Substituting this into the formula:

$Y=\frac{FL}{\left (\frac{πD2}{4}\right )\Delta L}=\frac{4FL}{πD^{2}\Delta L}$

To find the absolute error in $Y$, we need to find the relative error.

Since $F$ and $π$ are constants, the relative error in $Y$ is:

$\frac{\Delta Y}{Y}=\frac{\Delta L_{\text{scale}}}{L}+\frac{2\Delta D}{D}+\frac{\Delta (\Delta L)}{\Delta L}$

Where $\Delta L_{\text{scale}}$, $\Delta D$, and $\Delta (\Delta L)$ are the least counts of the respective measuring instruments.

The applied tensile force is $F=100\text{N}$,

The length of wire is $L=150\text{cm}=1.5\text{m}$,

The diameter of wire is $D=0.08\text{cm}=8\times 10^{-4}\text{m}$,

The extension in the length of wire is $\Delta L=0.5\text{cm}=5\times 10^{-3}\text{m}$.

$Y=\frac{4\times 100\times 1.5}{π\times (8\times 10^{-4})^{2}\times 5\times 10^{-3}}$

$Y=\frac{600}{π\times 64\times 10^{-8}\times 5\times 10^{-3}}=\frac{600}{π\times 320\times 10^{-11}}=\frac{6\times 10^{11}}{3.2π}$

$Y\approx 5.96\times 10^{10}\text{N/m}^{2}$

So, the error in measurement of Young’s modulus is $(\Delta Y)$:

$\Delta Y=Y\left [\frac{0.1}{150}+2\left (\frac{0.001}{0.08}\right )+\frac{0.001}{0.5}\right ]$

$\Delta Y=Y[0.00066+0.025+0.002]=Y[0.02766]$

$\Delta Y=(5.96\times 10^{10})\times 0.02766\approx 1.65\times 10^{9}\text{N/m}^{2}$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is $1.65$. Thus, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: The velocity of a particle is given as $⃗{v}=-x\hat{i}+2y\hat{j}-z\hat{k}$ m/s. The magnitude of acceleration at point (1, 2, 4) is $________ m/s^{2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The acceleration vector $⃗{a}$ is the total derivative of velocity with respect to time:

$⃗{a}=\frac{d⃗{v}}{dt}$

The velocity of the particle is given as $⃗{v}=-x\hat{i}+2y\hat{j}-z\hat{k}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

The x-component of velocity is $v_{x}=-x$

So, the x-component of acceleration is $a_{x}=\frac{dv_{x}}{dt}=\frac{dv_{x}}{dx}\times \frac{dx}{dt}=v_{x}\frac{dv_{x}}{dx}=(-x)\frac{d(-x)}{dx}=x$

The y-component of velocity is $v_{y}=2y$

So, the y-component of acceleration is $a_{y}=\frac{dv_{y}}{dt}=\frac{dv_{y}}{dy}\times \frac{dy}{dt}=v_{y}\frac{dv_{y}}{dy}=(2y)\frac{d(2y)}{dy}=(2y)(2)=4y$

The z-component of velocity is $v_{z}=-z$

So, the z-component of acceleration is $a_{z}=\frac{dv_{z}}{dt}=\frac{dv_{z}}{dz}\times \frac{dz}{dt}=v_{z}\frac{dv_{z}}{dz}=(-z)\frac{d(-z)}{dz}=(-z)(-1)=z$

Thus, the acceleration vector is $⃗{a}=x\hat{i}+4y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$.

At point $(1,2,4)$:

$⃗{a}=(1)\hat{i}+4(2)\hat{j}+(4)\hat{k}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$

The magnitude $|⃗{a}|$ is,

$|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{a_{x}^{2}+a_{y}^{2}+a_{z}^{2}}$

$|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{1^{2}+8^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{1+64+16}=\sqrt{81}$

$|⃗{a}|=9\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Therefore, the magnitude of acceleration at the given point is $9\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Therefore, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
The position of an object having mass 0.1 kg as a function of time $t$ is given as 
$⃗{r}=\left (10t^{2}\hat{i}+5t^{3}\hat{j}\right )$ m. At $t=1$ s, which of the following statements are correct?
A. The linear momentum $⃗{p}=\left (2\hat{i}+1.5\hat{j}\right )$ kg·m/s.
B. The force acting on the object $⃗{F}=\left (2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\right )$ N.
C. The angular momentum of the object about its origin $⃗{L}=15\hat{k}$ J·s.
D. The torque acting on the object about its origin $⃗{τ}=20\hat{k}$ N·m.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mass of object is $m=0.1kg$

The position of the object is given as $⃗{r}(t)=10t^{2}\hat{i}+5t^{3}\hat{j}$. We evaluate each statement at $t=1\text{s}$.

Linear momentum is defined as $⃗{p}=m⃗{v}$.

The velocity is defined as the rate of change of position,

$⃗{v}=\frac{d⃗{r}}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(10t^{2}\hat{i}+5t^{3}\hat{j})=20t\hat{i}+15t^{2}\hat{j}.$

At $t=1\text{s}$:

$⃗{v}=20(1)\hat{i}+15(1)^{2}\hat{j}=(20\hat{i}+15\hat{j})\text{m/s}$

So, the linear momentum of the object is,

$⃗{p}=0.1\times (20\hat{i}+15\hat{j})=(2\hat{i}+1.5\hat{j})\text{kg}\cdot \text{m/s}$

Thus, the statement A is correct.

Using Newton’s second law of motion the force is defined as $⃗{F}=m⃗{a}$.

The acceleration is the rate of change of velocity,

$⃗{A}=\frac{d⃗{v}}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(20t\hat{i}+15t^{2}\hat{j})=20\hat{i}+30t\hat{j}$

At $t=1\text{s}$,

$⃗{A}=20\hat{i}+30(1)\hat{j}=(20\hat{i}+30\hat{j})\text{m/s}^{2}$

$⃗{F}=0.1\times (20\hat{i}+30\hat{j})=(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j})\text{N}.$

Thus, the statement B is correct.

Angular momentum is defined as $⃗{L}=⃗{r}\times ⃗{p}$.

At $t=1\text{s}$, the position vector of the object is $⃗{r}=10(1)^{2}\hat{i}+5(1)^{3}\hat{j}=10\hat{i}+5\hat{j}\text{m}$.

$⃗{L}=(10\hat{i}+5\hat{j})\times (2\hat{i}+1.5\hat{j})$

$⃗{L}=10(1.5)(\hat{i}\times \hat{j})+5(2)(\hat{j}\times \hat{i})=15\hat{k}-10\hat{k}=5\hat{k}\text{Js}.$

Thus, the statement C is incorrect because in this statement the angular momentum is given as $15\hat{k}\text{Js}.$

Torque is defined as $⃗{τ}=⃗{r}\times ⃗{F}$.

$⃗{τ}=(10\hat{ı}+5\hat{ȷ})\times (2\hat{ı}+3\hat{ȷ})$

$⃗{τ}=10(3)(\hat{\mathrm{i}}\times \hat{\mathrm{j}})+5(2)(\hat{\mathrm{j}}\times \hat{\mathrm{i}})=30\hat{\mathrm{k}}-10\hat{\mathrm{k}}=20\hat{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{Nm}.$

Thus, the statement D is correct.

Since statements A, B, and D are correct, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: A planet ($P_{1}$) is moving around the star of mass $2M$ in the orbit of radius $R$. Another planet ($P_{2}$) is moving around another star of mass $4M$ in a orbit of radius $2R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_{2}$ and $P_{1}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a planet of mass $m$ orbiting a star of mass $M_{s}$ at a distance $r$, the gravitational force provides the necessary centripetal force for circular motion.


[IMG]


Centripetal Force = Gravitational Force

$\frac{mv^{2}}{r}=\frac{GM_{s}m}{r^{2}}$

So, the orbital velocity $v$:

$v=\sqrt{\frac{GM_{s}}{r}}$

The time period $T$ is the time taken to complete one full orbit of circumference $2πr$:

$T=\frac{2πr}{v}=\frac{2πr}{\sqrt{\frac{GMs}{r}}}=\frac{2πr\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{GM_{s}}}$

$T=\frac{2πr^{3/2}}{\sqrt{GM_{s}}}$

On squaring both sides

$T^{2}=\frac{4π^{2}r^{3}}{GM_{s}}\Rightarrow T\propto \sqrt{\frac{r^{3}}{M_{s}}}$

For planet $P_{1}$, $M_{s1}=2M$ and $r_{1}=R$.

$T_{1}\propto \sqrt{\frac{R^{3}}{2M}}$

For Planet $P_{2}$, $M_{s2}=4M$ and $r_{2}=2R$.

$T_{2}\propto \sqrt{\frac{(2R)^{3}}{4M}}=\sqrt{\frac{8R^{3}}{4M}}=\sqrt{\frac{2R^{3}}{M}}$

So, the ratio of time periods is:

$\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{\sqrt{\frac{2R3}{M}}}{\sqrt{\frac{R3}{2M}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2R^{3}}{M}\times \frac{2M}{R^{3}}}$

$\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\sqrt{4}=2$

Therefore, the ratio of the time periods of revolution of $P_{2}$ and $P_{1}$ is $2$. Thus, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as
$θ=\frac{5t^{4}}{40}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}$.
The angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is $_________$ rad$/s^{2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The angular velocity is the first derivative of angular displacement ($θ$) with respect to time ($t$).

$ω=\frac{dθ}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left (\frac{5t^{4}}{40}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right )$

$ω=\frac{5}{40}\times (4t^{3})-\frac{1}{3}\times (3t^{2})$

$ω=\frac{20t^{3}}{40}-t^{2}=\frac{t^{3}}{2}-t^{2}$

The angular acceleration ($α$) is the rate of change of angular velocity ($ω$) with respect to time.

So, angular acceleration is the derivative of angular velocity with respect to time.

$α=\frac{dω}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left (\frac{t^{3}}{2}-t^{2}\right )$

$α=\frac{1}{2}\cdot (3t^{2})-2t$

$α=1.5t^{2}-2t$

At $t=10$ seconds:

$α=1.5(10)^{2}-2(10)$

$α=1.5(100)-20$

$α=150-20=130\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Therefore, the angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is $130\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Thus, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance $C$. When it is half filled as shown in figure with a dielectric constant $K=5$, the percentage increase in the capacitance is $________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a parallel plate capacitor with plate area $A$, separation $d$, and air (or vacuum) between the plates, the capacitance is given by :

$\mathrm{C}=\frac{𝜖_{0}\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{d}}$


[IMG]


For a parallel plate capacitor with plate area A , separation d , and dielectric material with dielectric constant K between the plates, the capacitance is given by :

$C^{'}=\frac{K𝜖_{0}A}{d}$

When a dielectric slab of thickness $t=\frac{d}{2}$ and dielectric constant $K=5$ is inserted, the system is with two capacitors connected in series :


[IMG]


Capacitor 1 ($C_{1}$) is filled with dielectric, thickness $d_{1}=\frac{d}{2}$, and dielectric constant $K_{1}=5$.

So, the capacitance of capacitor 1 is

$C_{1}=\frac{K_{1}𝜖_{0}A}{d/2}=\frac{2K𝜖_{0}A}{d}=2KC=2\times 5C=10C$

Capacitor 2 ($C_{2}$) is filled with air, thickness $d_{2}=\frac{d}{2}$, and dielectric constant $K_{2}=1$.

So, the capacitance of capacitor 2 is

$C_{2}=\frac{K_{2}𝜖_{0}A}{d/2}=\frac{2K_{2}𝜖_{0}A}{d}=2K_{2}C=2\times 1C=2C$

For capacitors in series, the equivalent capacitance $C_{\text{new}}$ is:

$\frac{1}{C_{\text{new}}}=\frac{1}{C_{1}}+\frac{1}{C_{2}}$

$\frac{1}{C_{\text{new}}}=\frac{1}{10C}+\frac{1}{2C}=\frac{1+5}{10C}=\frac{6}{10C}$

$C_{\text{new}}=\frac{10}{6}C=\frac{5}{3}C\approx 1.6667C$

So, the percentage increase in capacitance is,

$\Delta %=\left (\frac{C_{\text{new}}-C}{C}\right )\times 100$

$\Delta %=\left (\frac{\frac{5}{3}C-C}{C}\right )\times 100=\frac{2}{3}\times 100\approx 66.67%$

Therefore, the percentage increase in capacitance is $66.67%$. Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: Heat is supplied to a diatomic gas at constant pressure. Then the ratio of $\Delta Q:\Delta U:\Delta W$ is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a diatomic gas (assuming no vibrational modes), the degrees of freedom $f=5$.

The molar specific heat at constant volume for diatomic gas is

$C_{v}=\frac{f}{2}R=\frac{5}{2}R$

The molar specific heat at constant pressure is

$C_{p}=C_{v}+R=\frac{5}{2}R+R=\frac{7}{2}R$

The heat supplied at constant pressure is

$\Delta Q=nC_{p}\Delta T=\frac{7}{2}nR\Delta T$

The change in internal energy is

$\Delta U=nC_{v}\Delta T=\frac{5}{2}nR\Delta T$

The work done at constant pressure is

$\Delta W=P\Delta V$

From ideal gas equation,

$PV=nRT\to P\Delta V=nR\Delta T$

So, the work done at constant pressure is

$\Delta W=P\Delta V=nR\Delta T=\frac{2}{2}nR\Delta T$

So, the ratio $\Delta Q:\Delta U:\Delta W$ is:

$\frac{7}{2}:\frac{5}{2}:\frac{2}{2}\to 7:5:2$

Therefore, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Two charged conducting spheres $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ of radii 8 cm and 18 cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ spheres are $E_{S1}$ and $E_{S2}$ respectively. The value of $\dfrac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two conducting spheres are connected by a wire, charge flows from one to the other until they reach the same electrical potential.

At equilibrium, the potential (V) of both spheres must be equal.

$V_{1}=V_{2}$

The potential at the surface of a conducting sphere of radius R and charge Q is given by:

$V=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{Q}{R}$

Therefore, for the two spheres:

$V_{1}=V_{2}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{Q_{1}}{R_{1}}=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{Q_{2}}{R_{2}}$

$\frac{Q_{1}}{R_{1}}=\frac{Q_{2}}{R_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}=\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}$

The electric field (E) at the surface of a conducting sphere is given by:

$E=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{Q}{R^{2}}$

So, the ratio $\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}$:

$\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}=\frac{\frac{1}{4π𝜖0}\frac{Q1}{R2 1}}{\frac{1}{4π𝜖0}\frac{Q2}{R2 2}}$

$\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}=\left (\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}\right )\times \left (\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}\right )^{2}$

Substituting the equilibrium condition $\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}=\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}$ into the electric field ratio:

$\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}=\left (\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right )\times \left (\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}\right )^{2}=\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}$

The radii are given as $R_{1}=8\text{cm}$ and $R_{2}=18\text{cm}$.

$\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}=\frac{18}{8}$

$\frac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}=\frac{9}{4}$

Therefore, the value of the ratio is $9/4$. Thus, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: The equation of a plane progressive wave is given by $y=5\cos π\left (200t-\frac{x}{150}\right )$ where $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ is in second. The velocity of the wave is $________ m/s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A plane progressive wave moving in the positive $x$-direction can be represented as:

$y=A\cos (ωt-kx)$

Where, $ω$ is the angular frequency, $k$ is the propagation constant (wave number).

The given equation is

$y=5\cos π\left (200t-\frac{x}{150}\right ).$

$y=5\cos \left (200πt-\frac{πx}{150}\right )$

By comparing this with $y=A\cos (ωt-kx),$ $ω=200π$ rad/s and $k=\frac{π}{150}$ rad/cm

Wave velocity is the distance travelled by the wave per unit time. It is related to angular frequency and wave number by the relation:

$v=\frac{ω}{k}$

Substituting the values of $ω$ and $k$:

$v=\frac{200π}{π/150}$

$v=200\times 150=30,000\text{cm/s}=300\text{m/s}$

Therefore, the velocity of the wave is $300\text{m/s}$. Thus, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Two short electric dipoles A and B having dipole moment $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$ respectively are placed with their axes mutually perpendicular as shown in the figure. The resultant electric field at a point $x$ is making an angle of $60^{\circ }$ with the line joining points $O$ and $x$. The ratio of the dipole moments $p_{2}/p_{1}$ is $_________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The direction of electric dipole is from negative charge to positive charge. So the direction of dipole moment for $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{P}_{1})$ is along $-\hat{\mathrm{i}}$; and that of dipole moment for $\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{P}_{2})$ is along $\hat{\mathrm{j}}$.


[IMG]


Dipole A ($p_{1}$) is oriented along the line OX. So, the point X lies on the axial line of dipole A. For a short dipole, the electric field at a distance r on the axial line is:

$E_{1}=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{2p_{1}}{r^{3}}$

This field $E_{1}$ acts along the direction of the dipole moment,

$⃗{E}_{1}=-\left (\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{2p_{1}}{r^{3}}\right )\hat{i}$

Dipole B ($p_{2}$) is oriented perpendicular to the line OX. So, point X lies on the equatorial line of dipole B. The electric field at a distance r on the equatorial line is:

$E_{2}=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{p_{2}}{r^{3}}$

This field $E_{2}$ acts in a direction opposite to the dipole moment $p_{2}$ (perpendicular to OX),

$⃗{E}_{2}=-\left (\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{p_{2}}{r^{3}}\right )\hat{j}$

The resultant electric field makes an angle $θ=60^{\circ }$ with the line OX.

$\tan θ=\frac{E_{2}}{E_{1}}$

Substituting the expressions for $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$:

$\tan 60^{\circ }=\frac{\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\dfrac{p_{2}}{r^{3}}}{\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\dfrac{2p_{1}}{r^{3}}}$

$\tan 60^{\circ }=\frac{p_{2}}{2p_{1}}$

$\sqrt{3}=\frac{p_{2}}{2p_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=2\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, the ratio of the dipole moments is $2\sqrt{3}$. Thus, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
For the given circuit (shown in part (A)) the time dependent input voltage $v_{in}(t)$ and corresponding output $v_{o}(t)$ are shown in part (B) and part (C), respectively. Identify the components that are used in the circuit between points X and Y.

[IMG]


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The output follows the input up to $+5\text{V}$ and $-5\text{V}$ and stays flat beyond them, so the circuit is a two-sided shunt clipper with clipping level $V_{Z}=5\text{V}$ in each half-cycle.

The given branch (ideal diode in series with the 5 V Zener, opposed) acts in one half-cycle only: its ideal diode is forward biased and the Zener breaks down, holding the output at 5 V in magnitude; in the other half-cycle its ideal diode blocks.

The branch between X and Y must clip the other half-cycle at 5 V, so it needs the same pair reversed: an ideal diode and a 5 V Zener in series with opposite orientations (anode joined to anode), so that in that half-cycle its diode is forward biased and its Zener is in breakdown.

A branch with a resistor (options A and C) does not hold the output at a constant level, and a diode and Zener pointing the same way (option D) conduct together in the forward direction and clamp the output at 0 V.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: When a coil is placed in a time dependent magnetic field the power dissipated in it is $P$. The number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $N$, $A$ and $r$ respectively. For a second coil number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $2N$, $2A$ and $3r$ respectively. When the first coil is replaced with second coil the power dissipated in it is $\sqrt{2}αP$. The value of $α$ is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Faraday's Law of Induction, the induced EMF in a coil is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux ($\Phi$).

The magnetic flux through the coil of number of turns N and area of cross-section A in magnetic field B is,

$\Phi =NBA$

So, the induced EMF is,

$ε=-\frac{d\Phi }{dt}=-NA\frac{dB}{dt}$

Let the rate of change of the magnetic field be $\frac{dB}{dt}=k$. Then:

$ε\propto NA$

If the radius of coil is $r_{\text{coil}}$ then $A=πr_{\text{coil}}^{2}\to r_{\text{coil}}=\frac{\sqrt{A}}{π}$

The resistance of the wire in the coil is given by:

$R=\frac{ρl}{A_{\text{wire}}}$

Where l is the total length of the wire and $A_{\text{wire}}$ is the cross-sectional area of the wire.

The total length of wire is l $=N\times (2π\times r_{\text{coil}})=N\times 2π\times \frac{\sqrt{A}}{π}=2N\sqrt{A}\to l\propto N\sqrt{A}$.

Cross-sectional area of the wire $A_{\text{wire}}=πr_{\text{wire}}^{2}$.

Thus, $R\propto \frac{N\sqrt{A}}{r_{\text{wire}}^{2}}$

Power dissipated in a resistive circuit is:

$P=\frac{ε^{2}}{R}$

Substituting the proportions for $ε$ and $R$:

$P\propto \frac{(NA)^{2}}{N\sqrt{A}/r_{\text{wire}}^{2}}=\frac{N^{2}A^{2}r_{\text{wire}}^{2}}{NA^{1/2}}=NA^{3/2}r_{\text{wire}}^{2}$

For the second coil: $N^{'}=2N,A^{'}=2A,r_{\text{wire}}^{'}=3r$.

So, the ratio of power dissipated is,

$\frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}=\frac{N^{'}}{N}\times \left (\frac{A^{'}}{A}\right )^{3/2}\times \left (\frac{r^{'}}{r}\right )^{2}$

$\frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}=(2)\times (2)^{3/2}\times (3)^{2}=2\times 2\sqrt{2}\times 9=36\sqrt{2}=α\sqrt{2}\Rightarrow α=36$

The value of $α$ is 36 . Thus, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in the following figures. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ respectively, then the ratio $\frac{B_{1}}{B_{2}}$ is $______$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For semi-infinite straight wire the field at a distance $r$ from wire is

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}$

The field at the centre of a circular arc subtending angle $𝜙$ is $B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}𝜙$, where $𝜙$ is in radians.

For a semicircle, $𝜙=π$, so $B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4r}$.

For system of current carrying wire (I), the direction of magnetic field using right hand rule is into the page due to semi-infinite wires and semi-circular wire.

Field from two semi-infinite wires is $2\times \frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}$

Field from semicircle is $\frac{μ_{0}I}{4r}$

As they act in the same direction, the net magnetic field is,

$B_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4r}+\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(π+2)$

The system of current carrying wires (II) consists of two straight wire and one semi-circular wire.

One of the straight wire is passing through the point Q, so the magnetic field due to the wire which passes through the same point where magnetic field is to be calculated is zero.

So, the magnetic field due to semi-infinite wire is $\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{4π\mathrm{r}}$

The magnetic field due to semi-circular wire is $\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{4\mathrm{r}}$

As they act in the same direction, the net magnetic field is,

$B_{2}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}+\frac{μ_{0}I}{4r}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(π+1)$

Therefore, the ratio of magnetic fields is,

$\frac{B_{1}}{B_{2}}=\frac{\frac{μ0I}{4πr}(π+2)}{\frac{μ0I}{4πr}(π+1)}$

The ratio of the magnetic fields is $\frac{2+π}{1+π}$. Thus, the correct option is (A).

text: For a thin symmetric prism made of glass (refractive index 1.5), the ratio of incident angle and minimum deviation will be $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a thin prism with a small prism angle (A), the angle of minimum deviation is given by,

$δ_{m}=(μ-1)A$

Where $μ$ is the refractive index of the glass, $μ=1.5$:

Putting the value of refractive index, $δ_{m}=(1.5-1)A=0.5A=\frac{A}{2}$

At the position of minimum deviation, the angle of incidence (i) is related to the prism angle (A) and the minimum deviation ($δ_{m}$) by

$i=\frac{A+δ_{m}}{2}$

Substituting the value of $δ_{m}=\frac{A}{2}$

$i=\frac{A+\frac{A}{2}}{2}=\frac{3A/2}{2}=\frac{3A}{4}$

So, the ratio of the incident angle (i) to the minimum deviation ($δ_{m}$) is,

$\frac{i}{δ_{m}}=\frac{3A/4}{A/2}=\frac{6}{4}=\frac{3}{2}$

Therefore, the ratio of the incident angle and minimum deviation is 3 : 2. Thus, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Refer the figure given below. $μ_{1}$ and $μ_{2}$ are refractive indices of air and lens material. The height of image will be $_______ cm$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With light travelling from the object towards the surface: $u=-40\text{cm}$, $R=-20\text{cm}$ (the centre C lies on the object side), $μ_{1}=1$, $μ_{2}=1.54$ and $h_{o}=2\text{cm}$.

Refraction at a spherical surface:

$\dfrac{μ_{2}}{v}-\dfrac{μ_{1}}{u}=\dfrac{μ_{2}-μ_{1}}{R}$

$\dfrac{1.54}{v}+\dfrac{1}{40}=\dfrac{0.54}{-20}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1.54}{v}=-\dfrac{1.08+1}{40}=-\dfrac{2.08}{40}$

$v=-\dfrac{1.54\times 40}{2.08}\approx -29.6\text{cm}$

The image is virtual and lies on the object side. Its magnification is

$m=\dfrac{μ_{1}v}{μ_{2}u}=\dfrac{1\times (-29.6)}{1.54\times (-40)}\approx 0.48$

$h_{i}=mh_{o}=0.48\times 2\approx 0.96\text{cm}\approx 1\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: For a certain metal, when monochromatic light of wavelength $λ$ is incident, the stopping potential for photoelectrons is $3V_{0}$. When the same metal is illuminated by light of wavelength $2λ$, then the stopping potential becomes $V_{0}$. The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission for the given metal is $αλ$. The value of $α$ is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The energy of an incident photon is $E=\frac{hc}{λ}$, where $h$ is the Planck’s constant, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum and $λ$ is the wavelength of incident light.

According to Einstein’s equation of photoelectric effect;

$\frac{hc}{λ}=𝜙+K_{\max }$

Where $𝜙$ is the work function is the minimum energy required to eject electron from the surface of metal, $\left (𝜙=\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}\right )$ and $K_{\max }=eV_{s}$ ($V_{s}$ is the stopping potential).

So, $\frac{hc}{λ}=\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}+eV_{s}$

Case 1: Wavelength is $λ$, stopping potential is $3V_{0}$.

$\frac{hc}{λ}=\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}+e(3V_{0})\ldots (i)$

Case 2: Wavelength is $2λ$, stopping potential is $V_{0}$.

$\frac{hc}{2λ}=\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}+eV_{0}$

$\Rightarrow 3\left (\frac{hc}{2λ}\right )=3\left (\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}\right )+3eV_{0}\ldots (ii)$

On subtracting equation (i) from equation (ii):

$\left (\frac{3hc}{2λ}-\frac{hc}{λ}\right )=\left (\frac{3hc}{λ_{0}}-\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}\right )+(3eV_{0}-3eV_{0})$

$\frac{hc}{2λ}=\frac{2hc}{λ_{0}}\to \frac{1}{4λ}=\frac{1}{λ_{0}}\to λ_{0}=4λ$

$\Rightarrow αλ=4λ\Rightarrow α=4$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 4. Thus, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
An electromagnetic wave travelling in x-direction is described by field equation
$E_{y}=300\sin ω\left (t-\frac{x}{c}\right )$.
If the electron is restricted to move in y-direction only with speed of $1.5\times 10^{6}$ m/s then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electric force acting on a charge $e$ is given by $⃗{F}=q⃗{E}$. The maximum force occurs when the electric field is at its peak $(E_{0})$:

$F_{e}(\max )=eE_{0}$

From the equation $E_{y}=300\sin ω\left (t-\frac{x}{c}\right )$, the peak electric field is $E_{0}=300\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$.

The magnetic force on a charge is $𝐅=q(⃗{v}\times ⃗{B})$, which has a maximum value of:

$F_{m}=evB_{0}$

Where $B_{0}$ is the peak magnetic field and $v$ is the speed of the electron $(1.5\times 10^{6}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s})$.

In an electromagnetic wave, the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by the speed of light $(c)$:

$c=\frac{E_{0}}{B_{0}}\to B_{0}=\frac{E_{0}}{c}$

The speed of light is $c\approx 3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

So, the ratio of maximum electric force to maximum magnetic force is:

$\frac{F_{e}}{F_{m}}=\frac{eE_{0}}{evB_{0}}=\frac{E_{0}}{vB_{0}}$

Substituting $B_{0}=E_{0}/c$ into the ratio:

$\frac{F_{e}}{F_{m}}=\frac{E_{0}}{v(E_{0}/c)}=\frac{c}{v}$

$\frac{F_{e}}{F_{m}}=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{1.5\times 10^{6}}$

$\frac{F_{e}}{F_{m}}=2\times 10^{2}=200$

Therefore, the ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces is $200$. Thus, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is $\frac{3h}{π}$, then the energy of the electron is $_____ eV$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Bohr's second postulate, the angular momentum (L) of an electron in a stationary orbit is quantized and given by :

$L=\frac{nh}{2π}$

The angular momentum is $L=\frac{3h}{π}$.

$\Rightarrow \frac{nh}{2π}=\frac{3h}{π}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{n}{2}=3$

$\Rightarrow n=6$

In the Bohr model, the total energy ($E_{n}$) of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom is the sum of its kinetic and potential energies. The energy in electron volts (eV) is derived as :

$E_{n}=-\frac{13.6}{n^{2}}\text{eV}$

For $n=6$:

$E_{6}=-\frac{13.6}{6^{2}}$

$E_{6}=-\frac{13.6}{36}$

$E_{6}\approx -0.3777\ldots \text{eV}$

Therefore, the energy of the electron is $-0.38\text{eV}$. Therefore, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: A liquid drop of diameter 2 mm breaks into 512 droplets. The change in surface energy is $α\times 10^{-6}$ J. The value of $α$ is $_______. ($Take surface tension of liquid = 0.08 N/m)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $R$ be the radius of the big drop and $r$ be the radius of each small droplet. Since volume is conserved during the process:

Volume of big drop $=512\times$ Volume of one small droplet

$\frac{4}{3}πR^{3}=512\times \left (\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}\right )$

$R^{3}=512r^{3}$

$R=(512)^{1/3}r=8r$

$r=\frac{R}{8}$

The diameter of bigger drop is $D=2\mathrm{mm}$, so $R=1\mathrm{mm}=10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$.

Thus, $r=\frac{10^{-3}}{8}\mathrm{m}$.

Surface energy is defined as surface tension $(T)\times (A)$.

Initial Surface Energy $U_{i}=T\times (4πR^{2})$

Final Surface Energy $U_{f}=512\times T\times (4πr^{2})$

$\Delta U=U_{f}-U_{i}=4πT\left (512\qquad r^{2}-R^{2}\right )$

Substituting $r=\frac{R}{8}$:

$\Delta U=4πT\left (512\left (\frac{R}{8}\right )^{2}-R^{2}\right )=4πT\left (\frac{512R^{2}}{64}-R^{2}\right )$

$\Delta U=4πT(8R^{2}-R^{2})=4πT(7R^{2})$

$\Delta U=28πTR^{2}$

The surface tension of liquid is $T=0.08\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$ and $R=10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$:

Putting the values,

$\Delta U=28\times \frac{22}{7}\times 0.08\times (10^{-3})^{2}$

$\Delta U=7.04\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}=α\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$

$α\approx 7$

The value of $α$ is $7$. Therefore, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: In single slit diffraction pattern, the wavelength of light used is 628 nm and slit width is 0.2 mm, the angular width of central maximum is $α\times 10^{-2}$ degrees. The value of $α$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

In single slit diffraction, the condition for the $n^{\text{th}}$ minimum is:

$a\sin θ=nλ$

Where, $λ$ is the wavelength of incident light on slit width of $a$.

For the first minimum $(n=1)$,

Assuming the angle $θ$ is small such that $\sin θ\approx θ$ (in radians):

$θ=\frac{λ}{a}$

The central maximum extends from the first minimum on one side to the first minimum on the other side.

Therefore, the total angular width $(2θ)$ in radians is:

$2θ=\frac{2λ}{a}$

To convert the angular width from radians to degrees, we multiply by $\frac{180}{π}$:

$\text{Width in degrees}=\left (\frac{2λ}{a}\right )\times \frac{180}{π}$

The wavelength of light is $λ=628\text{nm}=628\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$

The slit width is $a=0.2\text{mm}=0.2\times 10^{-3}\text{m}$

So,

$β=\frac{2\times 628\times 10^{-9}}{0.2\times 10^{-3}}\times \frac{180}{3.14}$

$β=\frac{1256\times 10^{-6}}{0.2}\times 57.32$

$β=6280\times 10^{-6}\times 57.32\approx 0.36\text{degrees}$

$=α\times 10^{-2}\text{degrees}=0.36\text{degrees}$

$36\times 10^{-2}=α\times 10^{-2}$

$α=36$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 36. Thus, the correct answer is 36.

text: A vessel contains $0.15 m^{3}$ of a gas at pressure 8 bar and temperature 140 °C with $c_{p}=3R$ and $c_{v}=2R$. It is expanded adiabatically till pressure falls to 1 bar. The work done during this process is $_________ kJ. (R$ is gas constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings ($\Delta Q=0$).

The adiabatic constant is the ratio of specific heats:

$γ=\frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}=\frac{3R}{2R}=1.5$

For an adiabatic process:

$P_{1}V_{1}^{γ}=P_{2}V_{2}^{γ}$

The initial pressure of the gas is $P_{1}=8$ bar,

The initial volume is $V_{1}=0.15\mathrm{m}^{3}$, and

The final pressure is $P_{2}=1$ bar:

$8\times (0.15)^{1.5}=1\times V_{2}^{1.5}$

$V_{2}^{1.5}=8\times (0.15)^{1.5}$

$V_{2}=8^{2/3}\times 0.15=(2^{3})^{2/3}\times 0.15=4\times 0.15=0.6\mathrm{m}^{3}$

So, the final volume of the gas is $0.6\mathrm{m}^{3}$

From the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta Q=\Delta U+W$. Since $\Delta Q=0$:

$W=-\Delta U=-nc_{v}(T_{2}-T_{1})$

Using the ideal gas relation $PV=nRT$,

$W=\frac{P_{1}V_{1}-P_{2}V_{2}}{γ-1}$

As $1$ bar $=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$:

So, $P_{1}=8\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ and $P_{2}=1\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$

Putting in the work done formula,

$W=\frac{(8\times 10^{5}\times 0.15)-(1\times 10^{5}\times 0.6)}{1.5-1}$

$W=\frac{1.2\times 10^{5}-0.6\times 10^{5}}{0.5}$

$W=\frac{0.6\times 10^{5}}{0.5}=1.2\times 10^{5}\mathrm{J}=120\mathrm{kJ}$

Therefore, the work done during this process is $120\mathrm{kJ}$. Thus, the correct answer is $120$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: 1 μC charge moving with velocity $⃗{v}=(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$ m/s in the region of magnetic field $⃗{B}=(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-5\hat{k})$ T. The magnitude of force acting on it is $\sqrt{α}\times 10^{-6}$ N. The value of $α$ is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The magnetic force acting on a charge $q$ moving with velocity $⃗{v}$ in a magnetic field $⃗{B}$ is given by :

$⃗{F}=q(⃗{v}\times ⃗{B})$

$⃗{F}=q\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ v_{x} & v_{y} & v_{z} \\ B_{x} & B_{y} & B_{z} \end{array}\right |$

$⃗{F}=1\times 10^{-6}\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \end{array}\right |$

Expanding the determinant:

$⃗{F}=1\times 10^{-6}(\hat{i}[(-2)(-5)-(3)(3)]-\hat{j}[(1)(-5)-(3)(2)]+\hat{k}[(1)(3)-(-2)(2)])$

$⃗{F}=1\times 10^{-6}[\hat{i}(10-9)-\hat{j}(-5-6)+\hat{k}(3+4)]$

$⃗{F}=1\times 10^{-6}[1\hat{i}+11\hat{j}+7\hat{k}]$

So, the magnitude $|⃗{F}|$ is:

$|⃗{F}|=10^{-6}\sqrt{1^{2}+11^{2}+7^{2}}$

$|⃗{F}|=10^{-6}\sqrt{1+121+49}$

$|⃗{F}|=\sqrt{171}\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{N}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{α}\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{N}=\sqrt{171}\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{N}$

$\Rightarrow α=171$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is $171$. Thus, the correct answer is $171$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: A uniform wire of length $l$ of weight $w$ is suspended from the roof with a weight of $W$ at the other end. The stress in the wire at $\frac{l}{3}$ distance from the top is $\left (\frac{W}{A}+\frac{2}{γ}\frac{w}{A}\right )$, where $A$ is the cross sectional area of the wire. The value of $γ$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Stress is force (tension) per unit cross-sectional area.

In a suspended wire with mass, the tension varies along its length because the wire must support the weight of the portion below it.

We need the stress at a distance $\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{3}$ from the top. This means the point is $\mathrm{l}-\frac{1}{3}=\frac{21}{3}$ distance from the bottom.


[IMG]


The total tension $T$ at this point must support the load weight $W$ attached to the bottom and weight of the portion

of the wire hanging below this point $(w^{'})$.

Since the wire is uniform, weight per unit length is $λ=\frac{w}{l}$.

The length of the wire below the point is $L_{\text{below}}=\frac{2l}{3}$.

$w^{'}=λ\times L_{\text{below}}=\left (\frac{W}{l}\right )\left (\frac{2l}{3}\right )=\frac{2w}{3}$

So, total tension $T$ at the point:

$T=W+w^{'}=W+\frac{2w}{3}$

So, the stress in wire is,

$σ=\frac{T}{A}=\frac{W+\frac{2w}{3}}{A}$

$σ=\frac{W}{A}+\frac{2w}{3A}=\left (\frac{W}{A}+\frac{2w}{γA}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}=\frac{2}{γ}$

$γ=3$

Therefore, the value of $γ$ is $3$. Thus, the correct answer is $3$.

text:
A tub is filled with water and a wooden cube $10\text{cm}\times 10\text{cm}\times 10\text{cm}$ is placed in the water. The wooden cube is found to float on the water with a part of it submerged in water. When a metal coin is placed on the wooden cube, the submerged part is increased by $3.87$ cm. The mass of the metal coin is $________$ gram.
(Take water density as $1\text{g/cm}^{3}$ and density of wood as $0.4\text{g/cm}^{3}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the wooden cube floats by itself, it is in equilibrium. The upward buoyant force ( $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}1}$ ) equals the downward weight of the wood ( $\mathrm{W}_{\text{wood}}$ ).


[IMG]


$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}1}=\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{wood}}$

The buoyant force is given by the weight of the displaced water :

$ρ_{\text{water}}\cdot V_{\text{submerged1}}\cdot g=m_{\text{wood}}\cdot g$

When a metal coin of mass $\mathrm{m}_{\text{coin}}$ is placed on top of the cube, the total weight increases. To remain in equilibrium, the cube must displace more water to provide an additional buoyant force ( $\mathrm{F}_{\text{extra}}$ ) equal to the weight of the coin.

Total Weight $=\mathrm{W}_{\text{wood}}+\mathrm{W}_{\text{coin}}$

Total Buoyant Force $=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}1}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{extra}}$

Since $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}1}=\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{wood}}$,

$F_{\text{extra}}=W_{\text{coin}}$

The extra buoyant force is equal to the weight of the additional volume of water displaced due to the coin.

Let $A$ be the surface area of the cube and $\Delta h$ be the increase in submerged depth.

So, the additional volume displaced is,

$\Delta V=A\cdot \Delta h$

$F_{\text{extra}}=ρ_{\text{water}}\cdot \Delta V\cdot g=ρ_{\text{water}}\cdot (A\cdot \Delta h)\cdot g$

$m_{\text{coin}}\cdot g=ρ_{\text{water}}\cdot (A\cdot \Delta h)\cdot g$

$m_{\text{coin}}=ρ_{\text{water}}\cdot A\cdot \Delta h$

The density of water is $ρ_{\text{water}}=1\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

The side of the cube is $s=10\mathrm{cm}$

So, the surface area is $A=s\times s=10\mathrm{cm}\times 10\mathrm{cm}=100\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

The increase in submerged depth, $\Delta h=3.87\mathrm{cm}$

As all the given values are in CGS units so the calculated mass will be in grams.

$m_{\text{coin}}=1\times 100\times 3.87\mathrm{g}$

$m_{\text{coin}}=387\mathrm{g}$

Therefore, the mass of the metal coin is 387 grams. Thus, the correct answer is 387.
